The general solution of the system is

$$
[\begin{aligned}x(t) \\ y(t)\end{aligned}]={c}_{1}{e}^{5t}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}{e}^{2t}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.
$$

The line that passes through the origin and is parallel to ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$ has the equation 

$$
y=x
$$

and the straight-line solutions of the form
${c}_{1}{e}^{5t}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$
lie on that line. 

Since ${e}^{5t}\to \infty $ as $t\to \infty ,$ these solutions approach $\text{infinity}$ as $t\to \infty .$

Let's add the solutions to the phase space.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14122747/assets/2ab8c69672acf64e93615960fdbb34445d4f81617cae16f90a8e4f30252607ba.png)

The line that passes through the origin and is parallel to ${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]$ has the equation 

$$
y=0
$$

and the straight-line solutions of the form
${c}_{2}{e}^{2t}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]$
lie on that line. 

Since ${e}^{2t}\to \infty $ as $t\to \infty ,$ these solutions approach $\text{infinity}$ as $t\to \infty .$

Let's add the solutions to the phase space.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14122747/assets/d1b7ffd22ad77fe94a994659fb7a091692b23bafb3012a705e964419fb71e8aa.png)

$$
0<{\lambda }_{2}<{\lambda }_{1}
$$

thus, ${\lambda }_{1}=5$ is the dominant eigenvalue.

Since the dominant eigenvalue is ${\lambda }_{1}=5,$ solutions become parallel to the straight-line solution containing the vector ${v}_{1}$ as they move away from the origin.
